newsitem.title: USA: Orange County sues Fuji Securities in wake of crisis.
newsitem.headline: Orange County sues Fuji Securities in wake of crisis.

text.p: California's Orange County has filed a $120 million-plus lawsuit against Fuji Securities Inc. for its alleged involvement in the county's financial collapse, county attorneys said Wednesday.
Orange County alleged that the unit of Fuji Bank Ltd. lent the county billions of dollars through complex financial transactions that the county maintains were illegal and improper for the county.
Fuji's attorney said the lawsuit was without merit. "Fuji did nothing which would give rise to liability under any legal theory whatsoever," Fuji's attorney, Mark Prager, said.

The suit, filed in U.S. Bankruptcy Court, seeks in excess of $120 million in damages from Fuji Securities for allegedly aiding breach of fiduciary duty, for violations of the state constitution, and for violations of the U.S. bankruptcy code.

"The county is aggressively pursuing its claims against Merrill Lynch and the other parties responsible for the county's financial collapse," said county attorney Michael Swartz of the firm of Hennigan Mercer and Bennett.

The county has already sued Merrill Lynch & Co., McGraw-Hill Cos Inc.'s Standard & Poor's Corp., Morgan Stanley Group Inc., KPMG Peat Marwick LLP, the Student Loan Marketing Association, bond counsel LeBoeuf Lamb Greene & MacRae and financial firm Rauscher Pierce Refsnes Inc.
Merrill Lynch has denied any wrongdoing and asserts that county officials were responsible for the financial losses. The other firms are also fighting the county lawsuits.
Following the Fuji Securities filing, county attorneys said they were considering additional legal action against other firms allegedly involved in the investment crisis.
Orange County filed for protection under Chapter 9 of the federal Bankruptcy Code on Dec. 6, 1994, after sustaining investment losses of more than $1.6 billion.
The county emerged from bankruptcy in June of this year.
